Recipes In the following recipes, the measured osmolarity is given. When composing solutions, we recommend that the osmolarity of the electrode solution (intracellular solution) be 10–20 mOsmol·L -1 lower than the extracellular solution. Animal preparation Glycerol-based modified artificial cerebrospinal fluid (GACSF) 225 mM glycerol 2.5 mM KCl 2 mM MgCl 2 ·6H 2 O 2 mM CaCl 2 ·2H 2 O 1.2 mM NaH 2 PO 4 21 mM NaHCO 3 10 mM HEPES 5 mM glucose Gassed with carbogen and adjusted to pH = 7.2 with NaOH, resulting in an osmolarity of 300–310 mOsmol/L. Artificial cerebrospinal fluid (ACSF) for current clamp recordings 125 mM NaCl 2.5 mM KCl 2 mM MgCl 2 ·6H 2 O 2 mM CaCl 2 ·2H 2 O 1.2 mM NaH 2 PO 4 21 mM NaHCO 3 10 mM HEPES 5 mM glucose Gassed with carbogen and adjusted to pH = 7.2 with NaOH, resulting in an osmolarity of ~310 mOsmol/L. Note: Block of glutamatergic and GABAergic synaptic input can be achieved by adding 0.1 mM picrotoxin, 0.05 mM DAP-5, and 0.01 mM CNQX to the ACSF. Artificial cerebrospinal fluid (ACSF) for Ca 2+ current recordings in voltage clamp 66.5 mM NaCl 20 mM CsCl 40 mM TEA-Cl 4 mM MgCl 2 ·6H 2 O 3 mM CaCl 2 ·2H 2 O 21 mM NaHCO 3 10 mM HEPES 5 mM Glucose 0.001 mM TTX 0.1 mM picrotoxin 0.05 mM DAP-5 0.01 mM CNQX Gassed with carbogen and adjusted to pH = 7.2 with HCl, resulting in an osmolarity of ~305 mOsmol/L. Patch clamp recordings Electrode solution (current clamp) 141 mM K-gluconate 10 mM KCl 10 mM HEPES 0.1 mM EGTA 2 mM MgCl 2 ·6H 2 O Adjusted to pH = 7.2 with KOH, resulting in an osmolarity of ~290 mOsmol/L. Electrode solution (voltage clamp: Ca 2+ currents) 146 mM CsCl 10 mM HEPES 0.1 mM EGTA 2 mM MgCl 2 ·6H 2 O Adjusted to pH=7.2 with CsOH, resulting in an osmolarity of ~290 mOsmol/L. Ionophore (amphotericin B) solutions Stock solution 100 μL of DMSO 4 mg of amphotericin B

steps.title: Prepare GACSF solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the following in water, gassed with carbogen (95 % O₂, 5 % CO₂), adjust pH to 7.2 with NaOH and bring the osmolarity to 300–310 mOsm·L⁻¹; keep the solution at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare ACSF for current‑clamp
steps.instruction: Dissolve the components, gassed with carbogen, adjust pH to 7.2 with NaOH (osmolarity ≈310 mOsm·L⁻¹). Optionally add synaptic blockers.

substeps.instruction: Optional: 0.1 mM picrotoxin, 0.05 mM D‑AP5, 0.01 mM CNQX

steps.title: Prepare ACSF for Ca²⁺ voltage‑clamp
steps.instruction: Dissolve the components, gassed with carbogen, adjust pH to 7.2 with HCl (osmolarity ≈305 mOsm·L⁻¹).

steps.title: Prepare electrode solution (current‑clamp)
steps.instruction: Mix the following, adjust pH to 7.2 with KOH (osmolarity ≈290 mOsm·L⁻¹).

steps.title: Prepare electrode solution (voltage‑clamp)
steps.instruction: Mix the following, adjust pH to 7.2 with CsOH (osmolarity ≈290 mOsm·L⁻¹).

steps.title: Make amphotericin B stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 4 mg amphotericin B in 100 µL DMSO, sonicate until the solution becomes uniformly turbid yellowish, vortex several times; keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare amphotericin‑containing electrode solution
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL microtube add 1 mL of the appropriate electrode solution, then add the volume of amphotericin B stock indicated in Table 1 (e.g., 4.5 µL for DA neurons in current clamp to obtain 180 µg·mL⁻¹). Shake by hand, add 1 % (0.1 mg · 100 µL⁻¹) tetramethylrhodamine‑dextran, keep on ice; the solution is usable for up to 3 h. Prepare a second microtube with 1 mL electrode solution only (tip‑fill).

substeps.instruction: Add defined µL of stock (see Table 1)
Place stock, tip‑fill, and amphotericin‑containing solutions on ice

steps.title: Anesthetize and dissect mouse brain
steps.instruction: Lightly anesthetize an adult mouse (12–14 weeks) with 5 % isoflurane, decapitate, cut a midline skull incision from caudal to rostral to the frontonasal suture, open the skull by rotating tissue‑forceps 180°, remove the brain with a spatula (≤30 s), and make two trim cuts (caudal and rostral) with a standard razor blade.

steps.title: Glue brain and cut slices
steps.instruction: Glue the brain onto the vibratome plate with Pattex Ultra Gel Matic, then cut 290 µm thick slices in 4 °C carbogenated GACSF using a Feather® razor blade; set vibratome speed to 0.06 mm·s⁻¹ and amplitude to 1.05 mm.

steps.title: Recover brain slices
steps.instruction: Incubate slices for 25–50 min in a recovery bath of carbogenated ACSF at 37 °C, then keep them at room temperature in carbogenated ACSF; use slices within 5 h.

steps.title: Transfer slices to recording chamber
steps.instruction: Place slices in the recording chamber, hold them down with a slice anchor, and superfuse continuously with carbogenated ACSF at the desired experimental temperature.

steps.title: Set up perforated‑patch (current‑clamp)
steps.instruction: Pull glass electrodes to 3–5 MΩ, fill tips with plain electrode solution (tip‑fill) and backfill with the amphotericin‑containing solution; place the electrode in the bath without positive pressure, approach the target cell with a slight positive pressure, release pressure as soon as a dent forms, then apply gentle negative pressure while monitoring a test pulse in voltage‑clamp mode (holding 0 mV, 5 mV amplitude). Continue until seal resistance exceeds 600 MΩ (may take up to 20 min). Switch to current‑clamp and monitor the perforation transition.

steps.title: Perform perforated‑patch voltage‑clamp
steps.instruction: After completing steps 1–7 of the current‑clamp setup, set the holding potential to –60 mV, continue applying 5 mV test pulses (every 10 s) in voltage‑clamp mode, and wait until the perforation reaches a steady state (stable current amplitude). Use higher amphotericin concentrations if required (see Table 1).

steps.title: Optional single‑cell labeling
steps.instruction: Use an electrode solution containing biocytin, perform the perforated‑patch experiment as described, then rupture the membrane patch by gentle suction or a large hyperpolarizing voltage pulse (~1–1.5 V) to allow tracer diffusion. Process the slice with standard histological or immunohistochemical methods.
